\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Tensorization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Reverse.Tensorization
\section{Overview}
Mixed power means permit a one-bit reverse inequality to extend to every cube dimension. Further noise increases every extended power mean with exponent less than one.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Minkowski inequality for finite sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finset_Lr_sum_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $s\subseteq I$ and $t\subseteq J$ be finite sets, let $r\ge1$, and let $a:I\times J\to\bbr$ satisfy $a(i,j)\ge0$ for $i\in s$, $j\in t$. Then $(\sum_{j\in t}(\sum_{i\in s}a(i,j))^r)^{1/r}\le\sum_{i\in s}(\sum_{j\in t}a(i,j)^r)^{1/r}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Mixed power-mean comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_minkowski_mixed}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finset_Lr_sum_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $0<q\le p$ and $F:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}\to[0,\infty)$. Writing $M_{r,z}u=(\E_z u^r)^{1/r}$ for uniform means, $M_{q,x}(M_{p,b}F(x,b))\ge M_{p,b}(M_{q,x}F(x,b))$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Tensorization of a reverse inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.tensorize_reverse_bonami_beckner}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_collapse_last, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_comm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_dim_zero, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_mono, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_dim_zero, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc_slice, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_minkowski_mixed, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{5}
Let $0<q<p$ and $0\le\rho\le1$. Suppose $M_q(T_\rho u)\ge M_p(u)$ for every nonnegative function $u$ on one bit. Then $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$ for every $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$, where $M_r(u)=(\E|u|^r)^{1/r}$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp positive-exponent reverse hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_bonami_beckner_positive_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_bonami_beckner_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.tensorize_reverse_bonami_beckner, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{1}
Let $0<q<p<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$. Every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$, where $M_r(u)=(\E|u|^r)^{1/r}$ under the uniform measure. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Power means increase under further noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_noise_antitone}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{7}
Let $q<1$, $0\le\rho\le\sigma\le1$, and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_q(T_\sigma f)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}
